title: AMC Javelin Engines by Year (1968–1974)
description: Every factory engine in the AMC Javelin by year, 1968–1974: the 232 and 258 sixes and AMC's 290, 304, 343, 360, 390 and 401 V8s, incl. the AMX models.
intro: The Javelin was American Motors' pony car from 1968 to 1974. It used AMC's own sixes and V8s, from the 232 to the 401, and from 1971 the AMX name was its top model.
Pick a year to see every engine offered that model year, with its code, rated horsepower and the trims it came in. Each engine links to its full specs.
The first Javelin ran from the 232 six to the 390 V8; the 1970 Mark Donohue model came with a 360 four-barrel.
The 1971 redesign added the 401 and made the AMX a Javelin model. Ratings are SAE net from 1972.

notes.1972|360|195: Single exhaust; 220 hp with dual exhaust.
